Physics: Coverage is well spread across Mechanics, Electromagnetism, Optics and Modern Physics, and almost all keys check out numerically with clean, non-overlapping options. The level, however, is skewed easy: a large majority are single-formula substitutions (q3, q13, q24, q39) with very few genuinely multi-concept items, so the section under-tests the upper end of BITSAT difficulty. Only the oblique-incidence radiation-pressure question needs replacement; the remaining fixes are wording/distractor polish.
[minor] Reword the opening noun stack "A 0.20 m amplitude spring–mass oscillator has spring constant 200 N m⁻¹" to "A spring–mass oscillator of amplitude 0.20 m has spring constant 200 N m⁻¹".

[minor] Distractor D pairs positive work done by the gas with an anticlockwise cycle, which is thermodynamically impossible and eliminable without the figure, so replace it with a consistent sign/direction combination (e.g. −600 J; clockwise).
[minor] "First half of a journey" does not specify half the distance or half the time, and the half-time reading gives 10 m s⁻¹ (option C), so state "first half of the total distance".

[major] Oblique-incidence radiation pressure (the cos²θ factor, plus the unstated assumption of specular rather than reversed reflection) is outside the BITSAT/NCERT treatment and makes both 5.0×10⁻⁷ N and 1.0×10⁻⁶ N defensible; rewrite for normal incidence or drop the item.

Chemistry: All forty keys and the numerical work check out (freezing point, half-life, gas-mixture pressure, Kohlrausch, ΔH–ΔU, Kp, de Broglie ratio and the empirical-formula calculation are all correct), and the spread across physical, inorganic and organic chemistry is reasonably broad with sensible BITSAT-level 90-second items. The level is tilted towards single-step recall and standard ordering questions, with only a handful (47, 64, 66, 67) demanding real multi-step reasoning, so a couple of the trivial recall items could be upgraded. The only fixes needed are the redundant VSEPR pair and the answer-cueing option structures in q47 and q53; the figure-dependent items (47, 52, 58, 72) must be checked against the final artwork before printing.

[minor] Only option A gives relationships that are consistent with its own stated configurations (B, C and D are internally contradictory), so the item can be answered without ever looking at the Fischer projections — make the distractors self-consistent so the figure is actually needed.

[minor] Options C and D are exact reverses of the same two-species comparison, which cues that the answer lies in that pair; replace one of them with a four-species sequence of the same form as A and B.

[minor] This tests exactly the same VSEPR shape-prediction skill as q48 (XeF4 geometry/hybridisation), so one of the two should be swapped for a different bonding topic (e.g. MO/bond order or dipole moment).

English Proficiency: The section covers the expected BITSAT spread — voice, agreement, prepositions, para jumbles, synonyms/antonyms, phrasal verbs and a two-question passage — and the passage-based items are well pitched. However, several vocabulary items (scarcity, mitigate, put off, resolute) are single-step recall with obviously wrong distractors, making the overall level a little easier than the actual paper, and the para jumble in q82 is denser than its 90-second budget warrants. Answer placement also needs attention: 12 of the 15 keys are option A, so redistribute the correct options before printing.

[minor] P opens with "This apparent abundance", which has no antecedent in the fixed opening sentence (it speaks only of widened access, not abundance), so add a reference to the volume of information available in the opening line.

[major] The "first sentence" is not uniquely determined: the chronological order 3–4–1–2 (inspection, shelves, declaration of readiness, then reopening after repairs) is at least as defensible as starting with sentence 2, so both B and C are supportable.

[major] The inline labels are misaligned with the options — the stem prints (A) after "The committee", (B) after "agreed on postponing" and "(D) No error" after "further evidence was available", while the option list maps (A) to "The committee" and (D) to "No error", leaving the final clause unlabelled.
[minor] The item is a word analogy (Annoyed : Furious :: Pleased : ___), not sentence completion, so the stem instruction/tag should be corrected to "Choose the word that completes the analogy".

Logical Reasoning: The section covers an appropriate spread of BITSAT logical-reasoning types (blood relations, classification, coding, analogy, dictionary order, series, syllogism) at an easy-to-moderate level, and the five fully specified verbal items all have correct, unique keys solvable well within 90 seconds. However, the three figure-based items (98, 99, 103) arrive with no artwork or blank options and must be supplied before printing, and the two alphabet-shift items (100, 101) overlap in the skill tested. Replacing one shift item and reframing the syllogism away from bank-exam "possibility/either-or" conventions would tighten both balance and level.
[major] All four options are empty and no figure is attached, so the item is unprintable and the key D cannot be verified.
[major] The figure carrying the number puzzle is only marked "[has figure]" but not supplied, so neither the pattern nor the key (13) can be checked.

[minor] This item tests exactly the same skill as Q100 (applying a fixed alphabet shift to each letter); replace it with a non-shift analogy (e.g. letter-position or reversal based) to avoid duplication.
[major] The folding/punch sequence and all four answer figures are missing (options are blank), leaving the item unsolvable as printed.

[minor] The "possibility" conclusion plus complementary either-or pair is a banking-exam convention rather than BITSAT style, and the term "architects" appears nowhere in the premises (making both statements irrelevant); reword using terms actually linked by the statements.

Mathematics: Coverage is broad and syllabus-faithful (algebra, coordinate geometry, calculus, vectors/3D, statistics, reasoning), and all keys check out numerically, with most items solvable in 45–80 s and only q124, q142 and q149 pressing the 90 s limit. The main defects are the outright duplication of the arctan derivative/tangent item (q116 vs q136) and a slight over-weighting of routine integration (five items) alongside very easy fillers such as q121 and q137. Replacing q136 with a different topic (e.g. logarithms, linear inequalities or a definite-integral property) and trimming one integration item would give a better-balanced, more discriminating section.

[minor] The points $(0,\pm5)$ are the ends of the minor axis (co-vertices), not vertices; reword as "vertices $(\pm13,0)$ and co-vertices $(0,\pm5)$" (or "axis endpoints") so the terminology is correct.

[minor] The matrix is specified in a roundabout way and the answer is requested in computing jargon ("row-major order"); state $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&1\end{pmatrix}$ explicitly and present the options as $2\times2$ matrices.
[major] This is essentially the same item as q116 (same function $\tan^{-1}\frac{2x}{1-x^2}$, same point $x=\frac12$, same computation $f'=8/5$), so one of the two must be replaced.
